title: First recording singers heard: Mamie Smith, Edith Wilson, Ma Rainey
summary: He recalls Mamie Smith and Edith Wilson and later played shows with Ma Rainey in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Who were some of the first singers you heard? Can you remember any famous blues singers or anyone coming here?
Well, the first two blues singers that...I mean, two record...recording singers that I remember of ever hearing were Edith Wilson and Mamie Smith.
Yeah. What kind of voice did Mamie have in those days? On her old records, it's hard to tell.
She had a kind of light voice. A keen voice.
Did you ever hear Ma Rainey in those days?
Oh, yeah, I heard Ma Rainey. In fact, it was I worked with her later on here. Well, you worked with her? A couple of days.
Did you travel with her show? Did she have a show?
No, I played a...one...a couple of shows with her. I played one at the Grand Theatre on 31st and State.
That was up in the later years.
